sentence: This project studies how a viral protein helps adeno-associated virus get secreted from cells during virus production and engineers improved versions of it.
This project studies how an interferon-stimulated gene restricts coronavirus replication and how coronaviruses form double-membrane vesicles in cells.
This project studies how differences in cognitive functioning relate to vulnerability for mood and anxiety disorders in young adults, using machine learning.
This project tests a nanotechnology therapy that turns fatty infiltration from rotator cuff tears into thermogenic fat to help muscle regenerate.
This project studies how sensory systems in different organisms detect, tell apart and combine cellular signals.
This project studies how an endoribonuclease that cuts host mRNA is controlled in viral infections and how it affects cell fate.
This project uses Medicare data and emergency department visit data to study how wildfire smoke exposure relates to cardiovascular disease in the Western US.
This project maps protein interactions between respiratory pathogens and host cells using proteomic methods, genetic screens and structural biology.
This project studies how a long noncoding RNA called Xist silences genes through histone modifications in the white-footed deermouse.
This project provides histology, microscopy and mass spectrometry services for studying eye tissue in vision research laboratories.
This project develops a plasma assay that detects non-coding RNAs and cytokines linked to lung cancer in African Americans.
This project studies how endothelial cells form a lumen during embryonic blood vessel development.
This project looks for genetic causes of neuropsychiatric symptoms such as aggression, psychosis and anxiety in Alzheimer disease.
This project refines CRISPR base editing that inactivates a mutant superoxide dismutase 1 protein, aiming at a gene therapy for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project develops a high-resolution imaging approach that scans across cerebral cortical layers to measure brain activity in humans.
This project builds a wireless microscope using event cameras to image voltage signals from large areas of the brain in unconstrained animals.
This project builds prediction models for chronic rejection and survival after lung transplantation using clinical data, lung microbiome and immune response signals.
This project provides a miniaturized two-photon microscope for studying brain activity in freely moving animals.
This project provides shared equipment for imaging the eye and testing how the visual system works in vision research.
